stories.headline: Lake sediment cores push back the date of the region's first farms

overview.label: What
overview.text: Pollen in three cores shows cereal crops 600 years earlier than thought.

overview.label: Why it matters
overview.text: It moves the start of settled farming into a wetter climate window.

summary: Researchers drilled three cores from a shallow glacial lake and counted pollen grains layer by layer.
Cereal pollen shows up roughly six centuries before the oldest known farm buildings nearby.
stories.fullText:
The team drilled the cores in winter, standing on the ice.

Each centimetre of mud covers about a decade. The pollen counts were checked by two labs working blind.

stories.headline: A small team rewrote its build system and cut CI time in half
summary: Caching test results by input hash did most of the work.
stories.fullText:
The old pipeline rebuilt every package on every push.

The new one hashes inputs and skips work it has already done.
